narrative: OMX30 opens with moderate tailwinds from continental European strength and positive global correlation (+0.482%), though momentum is cooling at the 50-MA (-0.0% differential). The index remains anchored in a bull regime (+3.6% above 200-MA) with MACD constructive, but technical breadth is cautious: RSI at 51.57 is neutral, ADX at 0.3 is weak with bearish DI bias reducing conviction, and Stochastic K/D in the 76–79 zone flags potential mean reversion. Yield backdrop is mixed—US 10Y +104bp helps banks but weighs on tech valuations, while oil's sharp -4.42% decline eases input cost pressure on industrials and consumer sectors. Risk positioning: we're 2% off the 52-week high in a low-volatility tape (VIX 17.1), making today's session vulnerable to any downside surprise on US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET.
morningBrief: OMX30 set for modest +0.3–0.5% open riding DAX/CAC coattails, but technical setup demands caution. We're at the 50-MA (3123 approx) where momentum flattens; support sits at 3085 (lower Bollinger band). ADX weakness at 0.3 cuts our conviction—treat any breakout moves with 30% reduced confidence. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) should see mild bid from higher yields, but NASDAQ's muted overnight (+0.27%) weighs on Ericsson/Hexagon sentiment. Oil's -4.42% is a net positive for industrials and consumer, but watch H&M carefully—while EUR/SEK weakness helps, budget woes in UK markets add downside risk. Key catalyst: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET; any surprise on labor will reprrice the 10Y and OMX30 sentiment. Positioning: Remain constructive but reduce risk into mid-morning; cover shorts only on a close above 3140.
